cohort: The study included 81 children aged 4 to 48 months with intussusception who were referred to Mousavi Zanjan Hospital.
finding: The prevalence of mesenteric adenitis was high (79%) in children with intussusception, and a statistically significant association was found between jelly stool and mesenteric adenitis, with all children with jelly stool having mesenteric adenitis.
mod_finding: No statistically significant association was observed between mesenteric adenitis and the type of delivery (P>0.05).
